purpose: Fixed CPU table for desktop Nika: every one of the 3^7 editable-label states and all 22 ordered CNN architectures.

dataset.training: The admitted nine train objects only. The four child labels use their canonical classroom labels in the pilot runs; the exhaustive table varies all seven editable labels, including the four child labels.
dataset.review: The three established review objects are evaluated after training and never supplied to the optimizer.
dataset.final: The three established final objects are evaluated after training and never supplied to the optimizer. This split was inspected in earlier work, so this artifact calls it a historically known holdout, not a new independent estimate.

frozenTraining.randomness: Dropout starts each fresh training run from the same fixed RNG sequence; its masks do not depend on editable labels or selected architecture when their tensor shapes are the same.
frozenTraining.hardware: NumPy CPU only; no GPU, endpoint, or new dependency

stateTable.keys: All 2187 base-3 strings in the editableIds order from prepare-data.py. The four child object IDs stay fixed, but their labels, like the three old labels, vary across the table.
stateTable.fixedTrainingLabels: The remaining two training IDs retain their canonical labels.
stateTable.runtimeLookup: Exact key only. Missing or malformed table data is an error; no fallback model or invented result is allowed.

initialization: Each one-block run starts from identical parameter arrays and fresh Adam moments. The two-block run copies the one-block initial w0, b0, head_w, and head_b; only its added w1 and b1 use the same fixed RNG stream. This isolates the added block from an accidental change to shared-layer initialization.
decisionRule: No seed, hyperparameter, split, or model choice may be changed after seeing review/final results. The repeat must be byte-identical in its serialized scientific result. The table is finite precomputation, not live training and not a search for a favorable score.
